title: Screen spec
description: What a stage writes before any JSX: which template, what goes in each slot, bound to which data (ui/specs/<screen>.json). An agent mints it, a person binds it, the checks run against the registry.

screen.description: Screen name, lower case, the same `screen:` used by parity scenarios, QA bugs and designc.json ui.screens.

intent.description: The ask, in plain words. What the reviewer checks the spec against.

data.description: Every piece of data the screen shows, with its shape and where it comes from.

source.description: Endpoint as 'METHOD /path' with :params, e.g. 'GET /api/bordereaux/:id'. The page test mocks it with the state's sample (MSW); request parity compares against it.

sample.description: Realistic sample value used by the preview. Shape must match. Keep it small: 3–8 rows.

slots.description: Keys are slot paths from the template ('main', 'header.actions'). Values are ordered placements.

preview.description: Not used by designc: approved previews are recorded in the ledger (ui_preview_approved).

component.description: React component name of the generated page.

states.description: The screen's state graph: the spine. Acceptance `states`, scenario step `state:` and QA bug `state:` use these names. Required for a UI element: ready, loading, empty, error (forbidden when reached through an authenticated relationship).

data.description: Sample overrides for this state, by data key. null means no value (nothing selected), not loading.

error.description: Error message passed to components bound to a failed key.

pending.description: Data keys still loading in this state. Components bound to them get loading: true.

failed.description: Data keys whose request failed. Components bound to them get error (the state's error message).

commits.description: The action writes (Save, Apply, Delete). Cannot be recorded read-only; needs a mock and --allow-writes.

file.description: Path of the page's source file in the app. The page test is always generated from the spec and imports this.

host.description: Marks this spec as an overlay (a hosted spec): the screen and state it opens over, and the placement id in that screen that opens it. Cross-spec checks live in renderer/ui.js hostRules.

screen.description: Screen name of the host spec (ui/specs/<screen>.json).

state.description: The host state the overlay is open in.

anchor.description: Placement id in the host spec whose locator opens the overlay (the host has a click transition into the state on it).

id.description: Stable id, used as data-ui-id in the generated code so CI can map DOM back to spec.

bind.description: Data prop name → key in the spec's data section.

why.description: One line: why this component for this data. Helps the reviewer catch type-valid-but-wrong choices.

locator.description: Accessible role and name the element will have. Joins the placement to acceptance locators, parity recordings and the UI graph.

action.description: One step a scenario can perform, same verbs as parity scenarios.

event.description: Not a user action: 'data arrives', 'request fails'.
